---
title: "Harmonising variables"
---

Harmonisation maps a dataset's [tidied table](tidy-scripts.qmd) onto the project [dataschema](../reference/dataschema.qmd), so that every study contributes the same variables with the same meanings.
It is entirely table-driven: you edit CSV files, not R scripts.

The files involved:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `harmonisation/dataschema.csv` | The shared schema — one row per harmonised variable (shown in the [Dataschema reference](../reference/dataschema.qmd)) |
| `harmonisation/datasets/BPIPD-<id>/variables.csv` | How *this* dataset derives each schema variable |
| `harmonisation/lookups/*.csv` | Shared recode tables reused across studies (e.g. ethnicity) |
| `harmonisation/datasets/BPIPD-<id>/lookups/*.csv` | Large one-off recode tables specific to this dataset |

## variables.csv

One row per dataschema variable, in dataschema order.
The template copy starts with every variable set to `in_progress`; harmonising a dataset means working through the rows.

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `target_variable` | The dataschema variable being derived. Every non-system schema variable must have a row (`dataset_id`, `dataset_name` and `st_measure_id` are injected by the pipeline). |
| `status` | How well the study supports this variable (table below). |
| `source_columns` | Which tidied columns the mapping uses — documentation for reviewers, not executed. |
| `expression` | R code that computes the value (required unless the status says the variable can't be derived). |
| `notes` | Anything a reviewer needs: assumptions, DOIs, caveats. |
| `lookup_table` | Basename of a lookup CSV this expression uses, if any (e.g. `ethnicity` for `harmonisation/lookups/ethnicity.csv`). |
| `measure` | Optional; blank for the dataset's primary measure. A tag such as `diary` marks rows that map the screen-time variables again for an additional measure — see [Several screen-time measures](#several-screen-time-measures). |

A few illustrative rows (the column names are fictional, but the shapes mirror real mappings in the project):

```csv
target_variable,status,source_columns,expression,notes,lookup_table
participant_id,compatible,serial,as.character(serial),Assume serial is the participant ID,
wave,unavailable,,,Cross-sectional study,
data_year,inferred,,2016,Not in the data; taken from the study protocol,
sex,compatible,sex_raw,"recode_values(haven::as_factor(sex_raw), ""F"" ~ ""Female"", ""M"" ~ ""Male"")",Convert labels to harmonised values,
```

## Statuses

Statuses follow the [Maelstrom Research](https://www.maelstrom-research.org/) harmonisation vocabulary:

```{r}
#| label: status-table
statuses <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Status, ~Meaning, ~Evaluated,
  "compatible",
  paste(
    "The study variable can generate the target with an explicit,",
    "scientifically defensible transformation and without meaningful",
    "loss of meaning."
  ), "Yes",
  "partial",
  paste(
    "The study only supports part of the target construct, or the",
    "harmonised value requires a simplification that should be",
    "interpreted with caution."
  ), "Yes",
  "proximate",
  paste(
    "A categorical subtype of partial: the study captures a close but",
    "not fully equivalent category structure."
  ), "Yes",
  "inferred",
  paste(
    "The value is derived from study metadata or surrounding context",
    "(e.g. a fixed collection year from the study's publication)",
    "rather than a like-for-like study variable."
  ), "Yes",
  "incompatible",
  paste(
    "Related information exists, but it cannot be transformed into a",
    "defensible version of the target variable."
  ), "No — output is NA",
  "unavailable",
  "The study does not collect the required information.",
  "No — output is NA",
  "in_progress",
  "The mapping has not been completed yet (the template default).",
  "No — output is NA"
)
knitr::kable(statuses)
```

```{r}
#| label: status-drift-check
#| include: false
# Fail the site build if this table drifts from the pipeline's status set.
source("../R/config.R")
stopifnot(setequal(statuses$Status, bp_harmonisation_status_values()))
```

Rows with an "evaluated" status must have an `expression`; rows with the other three statuses are skipped and the variable is filled with typed `NA` values for that dataset.
How to choose between the statuses, including incompatible versus unavailable, is set out under [Harmonisation conventions](#harmonisation-conventions).

## Writing expressions

An expression is a single R expression evaluated against the tidied table.
Its result is recycled to the table's row count (so a constant like `2016` is fine) and cast to the schema's declared type.
Inside an expression you can reference:

- **columns of the tidied table** directly by name (`serial`, `sex_raw`);
- `tbl` or `analysis_base` — the whole tidied table, if you need it;
- `spec` — the parsed `dataset.yaml` (e.g. `spec$dataset_id`);
- `lookup_<name>` — any lookup table named in the row's `lookup_table` column (e.g. `lookup_ethnicity`).

Expressions run in a **sandboxed environment**, not your R session.
Bare function calls resolve from base R plus this curated allowlist:

```{r}
#| label: allowlist-table
source("../R/helpers.R")
source("../R/harmonise/harmonisation_functions.R")
fns <- bp_harmonisation_functions()
origin <- vapply(
  fns,
  function(fn) {
    env_name <- environmentName(topenv(environment(fn)))
    if (env_name %in% c("R_GlobalEnv", "")) "pipeline helper" else env_name
  },
  character(1)
)
allowlist <- tibble::tibble(
  Function = paste0("`", names(fns), "()`"),
  From = origin
)
knitr::kable(allowlist)
```

Namespaced calls such as `haven::as_factor()` also work for anything not on the list.
If an expression calls a bare function that is neither base R nor allowlisted, the test suite fails with a message telling you to either namespace it or add it to `bp_harmonisation_functions()` (`R/harmonise/harmonisation_functions.R`) — extending the allowlist is a one-line change, reviewed like any other.

Typical recodes use `recode_values()` with formula syntax:

```r
recode_values(
  haven::as_factor(sex_raw),
  "F" ~ "Female",
  "M" ~ "Male"
)
```

## Lookup tables

Three tiers, from smallest to largest:

1. **Inline** — short, study-specific recodes stay in the expression itself (like the `sex` example above).
2. **Shared lookups** (`harmonisation/lookups/*.csv`) — recurring recodes that should be reviewed centrally, such as ethnicity or maternal education.
   These must have the columns `dataset_id`, `target_variable`, `source_value`, `harmonised_value`, `mapping_status`, `notes`, with one row per source value per dataset.
3. **Dataset lookups** (`harmonisation/datasets/BPIPD-<id>/lookups/*.csv`) — mappings too large to read inline but not shared across studies.
   At minimum they need `source_value` and `harmonised_value` columns.

To use one, put its basename in the row's `lookup_table` column and call `lookup_values()` with the matching `lookup_<name>` object.
For example, an `ethnicity` row with `lookup_table` = `ethnicity`:

```r
lookup_values(
  haven::as_factor(ethnicity_raw),
  lookup_ethnicity,
  dataset_id = spec$dataset_id,
  target_variable = "ethnicity"
)
```

The `dataset_id`/`target_variable` arguments filter a shared lookup down to this dataset's rows; omit them for a dataset-specific lookup.
A lookup name must exist in exactly one of the two locations — the validator errors if it is missing from both or present in both.

## Several screen-time measures

A study sometimes measures screen use more than once per occasion: a questionnaire and a time-use diary, or a parent report and a child report.
The harmonised table keeps one row per participant per wave *per measure*, and the system variable `st_measure_id` says which measure a row carries.

The untagged rows of `variables.csv` describe the dataset's primary measure, and every row they produce has `st_measure_id = "primary"`.
An additional measure is a block of rows tagged in the `measure` column with a short lower-case token (`diary`, `parent`, `child`, `device`):

```csv
target_variable,status,source_columns,expression,notes,lookup_table,measure
st_measure_type,inferred,,"""Continuous""",Diary slots are 10 minutes,,diary
st_measure_name,inferred,,"""Time use diary""",,,diary
st_responder,inferred,,"""Self""",The child completes the diary,,diary
st_watch_wd,compatible,tud_tv_mins_wd,tud_tv_mins_wd / 60,Minutes to hours,,diary
```

For each tag the harmoniser evaluates the tagged rows against the same tidied table and emits one extra row per participant-wave, with `st_measure_id` set to the tag.
Only the screen-time variables can be tagged; every other variable in those rows is copied from the primary rows.
Screen-time variables the measure does not map are `NA` in its rows rather than inherited, and a participant-wave with no screen-time quantity for the measure gets no row at all.
Every measure block must map `st_measure_type`, `st_measure_name` and `st_responder`, so the rows say what instrument and respondent they came from.
Only the numeric screen-time rows count as screen-time quantities: the character descriptor `st_violent_measure` may be mapped in a block, but like those three it never keeps a row or a respondent on its own.
On primary rows, the harmoniser sets `st_responder` to `NA` wherever every screen-time quantity is missing, because no one reported screen use there; `st_measure_type` and `st_measure_name` describe the instrument and stay filled.

The tidier stays one row per participant-wave: the extra measure arrives as extra columns (`tud_tv_mins_wd`, `tv_hours_parent`), and the mapping decides which measure they belong to.
Analyses that want the old one-row table filter on `st_measure_id == "primary"`; analyses that compare instruments use `st_measure_name` and `st_responder` as covariates.

## Harmonisation conventions

These rules apply across rows; rules for a single variable sit in its dataschema notes.
Dataschema notes refer to the named rules below in bold (for example the **SDQ rule**).

### Statuses

- Choose the status in this order: unavailable if nothing on the row's construct is in the supplied data; incompatible if an item on the construct is in hand but cannot become the row; inferred if the value is a constant or descriptor taken from documentation, file or wave labels, or row position; otherwise compatible, partial or proximate by fidelity.
- Incompatible covers items the schema routes to another row, items already used on another row and items asked only of a subsample; unavailable is only for 'nothing related in hand' or 'Not in the supplied extract.'
- Typical reasons for incompatible are a wrong metric (frequency, yes/no, rank, most-used choice or ownership instead of duration), a wrong rating format (truth, agreement, intensity or distress instead of frequency), a wrong respondent and bundled content.
- An incompatible row names the rejected item in `source_columns`, and its note says why it fails and which row holds it.
- A row that only adds a weekday/weekend, device or at-school split the study never made is unavailable, whatever the parent row's status ('No weekday/weekend split.', 'No device split; see \<row>.', 'No item on use at school.').
- A named-instrument row is unavailable when that instrument, or a version of it, was not given to that informant ('\<instrument> not administered; see \<row>.'), and incompatible only when a version was given but cannot be scored.
- A generic scale row with only single items, or only an item subset of a broader instrument not given for the construct, is incompatible, and its note points to any row that holds them; the subject self-concept rows are one exception and take a single item, or an item subset of a broader instrument, on their subject as partial, and the parental mediation rows (`fam_mediation_restrict`, `fam_mediation_active`, `fam_mediation_monitor`) are another and take a single graded item, or a study's own graded items, as partial.
- A composite that can be derived at analysis from mapped rows is unavailable ('Derive at analysis from \<rows>.').
- A named instrument given only to another informant leaves this informant's row unavailable.
- A single-item `_self` row with only a parent- or teacher-rated analogue is incompatible, item named.
- A generic `_self` scale row with only a parent-, carer- or teacher-rated scale on its construct in hand is incompatible, naming the scale and the row that holds it.
- Compatible needs a note that describes no loss; a note saying 'only', 'undercount', 'narrower', 'bundled' or 'may include' means partial at best.
- A schema note that sends an item to another row forbids mapping it here.
- Partial covers part of the construct, pooled or coarser sources, subsets on named rows, and lifetime or unstated recall.
- Proximate is only for categorical rows whose sole loss is the category structure; binary and double rows use partial, and so does a row that loses both scope and categories.
- Three binary or double rows are exceptions and take proximate: a parent's statements on what the child's media use costs (perceived-effects items) on `beh_problematicuse_parent`, an onset or menarche item alone on `hlth_puberty_status`, and a frequency item on how often health or emotional problems limit activities on `hlth_disability`.
- Inferred is for constants and for descriptor rows (`st_measure_type`, `st_measure_name`, `st_responder`, `parent_respondent`, every `*_measure` row), unless a source column records the value directly, such as a who-answered variable (compatible).
- A descriptor row whose score row is unavailable is unavailable too ('See \<row>.').
- A parent's or carer's own characteristic used for the child is proximate.
- A value derived from a recorded variable is never inferred.
- Coverage never sets the status: a row mapped for some waves, ages or grades takes the status its mapped values deserve, and its note starts with the coverage ('2018-2023 only.').
- A dataset that mixes waves with per-row values and waves with assigned values takes the weaker status and names the affected waves.
- A bounded recall window (two weeks to 12 months, or 'this school year') leaves the status unchanged, even when it changes between waves; a lifetime or unstated window is partial.
- On the binary prevalence rows for suicidal ideation, suicide attempt and depression screening, any recall other than 12 months is partial.
- A weaker item fills waves the better item missed only on score rows standardised within wave (partial, waves in notes).
- Yes/no prevalence rows keep the better series alone; they never splice in a different recall window or a pooled item.
- Every unavailable or incompatible row has a one-line note.
- Standard notes are 'Not collected.', 'Not in the supplied extract.', 'No weekday/weekend split.', 'No device split; see \<row>.', 'No item on use at school.', '\<instrument> not administered; see \<row>.', 'Derive at analysis from \<rows>.', 'Not an Australian dataset.', 'Hukou not asked.', 'Not a randomised trial.', 'Single collection occasion.', 'Not a survey sample.' (survey design rows), 'One participant per family.' (`family_id`), 'Single sample.' (`sample_component`) and 'No cognitive testing.' (cognitive test rows in studies that gave no test; not the speech or language diagnosis rows or the parent-report early-language row)
- An unavailable note never describes an item in hand and never lists the study's other instruments.
- `source_columns` lists tidied column names, comma-separated, with no ranges and no raw-file names.
- Notes quote the item wording and record the reporter, the waves and the recall period.
- A row accepts any informant unless its name or description says otherwise; record the informant.
- `parent_respondent` records the adult who answered the parent or carer questionnaire on the occasion (the screen-time reporter where parent components had different respondents, else the main parent interview); an item recording only the respondent's sex reads female as Mother and male as Father (proximate), and the value is never carried across waves; where two parents each report on one occasion, the family parent-report rows take the parent it records.
- Notes state the rule applied and never cite another dataset as precedent.
- A choice settled for one dataset only stays in that dataset's notes.
- Dataschema text is public: it never names real datasets or their source columns.
- Before finishing, re-read every note against its status.

### Screen time

- Every `st_*` quantity is hours per day as a double.
- The violent-content index rows (`st_violent_watch_index`, `st_violent_game_index`) are the one exception: they hold the study's exposure index in its own metric, standardised within dataset at analysis.
- Minutes / 60; hours and minutes h + m / 60; weekly totals / 7; a total for both weekend days / 2.
- Clear negative and sentinel codes to NA before any arithmetic.
- Bands: 'none' = 0, closed bands at their midpoint, 'less than 1 hour' = 0.5, sub-hour bands at their midpoint ('less than 30 minutes' = 0.25), point labels ('about 2 hours') at the stated value.
- An open top band takes the lower bound its label states ('5 or more' = 5, 'more than 7 hours' = 7).
- A point label below the top band ('about 4 hours') is read as a band of plus or minus half an hour, so 'more than 4 hours' takes 4.5.
- Write the top-band value into the row's notes.
- Recode raw bands per wave where band sets differ, and use study-derived hours only if they follow these rules.
- Weekday and school-day items map to `_wd`; weekend and non-school-day items, holidays included, map to `_we`.
- The unsuffixed row is (5 × wd + 2 × we) / 7, and only when both are mapped for the same wave.
- Weekday-only items fill `_wd` only; the unsuffixed row is incompatible ('Weekday items only; no usual-day value.') and `_we` is unavailable.
- Usual-day items fill the unsuffixed row only; `_wd` and `_we` are unavailable ('No weekday/weekend split.').
- With no day split, `_wd` and `_we` are unavailable even when the unsuffixed row is incompatible.
- `*_school` rows take use while at school only; an item about a whole school day goes to `_wd`.
- **Non-users:** 0 when a filter establishes non-use (routed past the item, 'not at all', or no device with use unanswered); NA when not asked or not answered; a filter never overrides a reported duration.
- Keep values above 24 hours; they are excluded at analysis, with a sensitivity analysis that keeps them.
- **Day-of-use rule:** minutes on a day of use are multiplied by the share of days used (days per week / 7) and marked partial; minutes with no frequency answer are NA.
- Frequency-only, rank, most-used, yes/no and ownership items give no hours, so the row is incompatible, item named.
- Sum only sub-categories of one row (DR-0002): devices within gaming, sources within watching, gaming and non-gaming within computer, activities within one device, locations within one content row.
- Write 'Sum of A, B (DR-0002)' in the notes of a summed row.
- Never sum across watching, gaming, computer, phone, social media or internet, including into `st_total`, whoever did the summing.
- Screen-time sums use `+`, with routed-out parts written as explicit zeros; `sum_nonmissing()` only where the instrument scores blanks as zero.
- A skipped part is never scored as zero, so it leaves the sum NA.
- An item may feed its umbrella row as a DR-0002 part, but never stands in for a broader or sibling row: texting is not `st_phone`, phone gaming is not `st_phone`, internet time is not `st_total`.
- A single-activity item mapped to its content row leaves the device row incompatible.
- A bundled item maps to one row as partial, and every other row it touches is incompatible, naming the item and the row it went to.
- Social media with messaging goes to `st_socmedia`.
- Gaming with other non-school computer use goes to `st_game`, and `st_comp` is incompatible.
- Gaming or computer items whose examples name social media never map to `st_game*`.
- Phone with tablet goes to `st_phone` or `st_game_phone` (partial), and the tablet row is incompatible.
- Computer with tablet as one response option goes to `st_tablet` or `st_game_tablet` (partial), and the computer row is incompatible.
- Residual 'other online or device use' goes to `st_internet`.
- A bundled or residual item is never added to a row that already has a direct item, nor spliced onto a row that a different item fills in other waves; name it as unused.
- A social-media item whose examples name video-sharing platforms is not bundled with watching.
- Watching pooled with gaming, computer or internet use goes to `st_total`.
- An item that would go to `st_total` but is restricted to leisure (screen use for reasons other than school work), with no paired school-work item, goes to `st_leisure`, and `st_total` is incompatible ('Leisure only; see st_leisure'); an all-device item split into a school-work and a leisure part fills `st_educational` and `st_leisure`, and their sum fills `st_total`.
- Paired school-work and leisure items asked over one multi-device scope are summed into `st_total` as the two purpose parts, partial where the scope leaves out devices or the school part pools paid work; a pair on one device, or on the internet alone, follows that device's row or `st_internet` (DR-0002), and `st_total` is incompatible.
- A leisure item on several devices that leaves out TV or other screens is partial on `st_leisure`; a leisure item on one device or one activity stays on that row, and `st_leisure` is incompatible; a residual item asked beside separate watching or gaming items stays on `st_internet`.
- Under a pooled multi-device gaming item, the device rows are unavailable ('No device split; see st_game.'); pooling activities within one device is bundling and stays incompatible.
- `st_game` covers gaming on any device.
- A gaming item that names devices and leaves out phones and tablets is partial whatever its year; an item naming no device is compatible.
- An item limited to the TV set (broadcast TV, or videos and DVDs on the set) is partial on `st_watch`; the test is the device, not the word 'videos'.
- A computer item that excludes games goes to `st_comp_nongaming`; other purpose-restricted device items are partial.
- Internet time on one device maps to that device's row as partial.
- Hours of watching or gaming classified as violent (an item on violent programmes or games, or the hours of named titles classified as violent, summed over titles) go to `st_violent_watch` or `st_violent_game`; a violent-only item never stands in for `st_watch` or `st_game`, which are incompatible ('Violent games only; see st_violent_game').
- Violent gaming hours split by day go to `st_violent_game_wd` and `st_violent_game_we` under the day rules above, and `st_violent_game` then takes their 5:2 mean.
- Violent watching hours split by day go to `st_violent_watch_wd` and `st_violent_watch_we` in the same way, and `st_violent_watch` then takes their 5:2 mean.
- On those hours rows a violence content descriptor, the study's violent/non-violent coding or a yes/no rating classifies a named title, and a violent genre classifies it as partial; a graded violence rating or an age-rating level alone never does, and weighted by time or frequency it goes to the index rows.
- An index that weights named titles' violence ratings by how often or how long each is used goes to `st_violent_watch_index` or `st_violent_game_index`; the rater (respondent, rating board or study) goes in `st_violent_measure` and does not change the status, and a study index pooled over watching and gaming is not used.
- Hours of watching programmes, DVDs or videos made to educate children go to `st_educontent_watch` and its `_wd` and `_we` rows, classified by the item's wording, the study's coding of titles or diary episodes, or a yes/no rating per title; a prosocial-only code or an infant-directed video does not make a programme educational.
- An item on educational programmes only never stands in for `st_watch` or `st_educational`, which are incompatible for it; asked beside other programme items it is a DR-0002 part of `st_watch`, and screen use for school work stays on `st_educational`.
- Study or homework time that does not name screens goes to `acc_homework_time` and is incompatible on the `st_*` rows, except during fully remote schooling (partial on `st_educational`).
- A row that splices instruments with a documented level shift is partial.
- Screen-time doubles never use proximate.
- `st_measure_type` records the format behind the row's core `st_` variables.
- `st_measure_name` takes one controlled label: a published instrument name, 'Time use diary', 'Custom' or 'Unknown'.
- `st_measure_type` and `st_measure_name` are filled wherever the instrument was administered; the harmoniser sets only `st_responder` to NA on primary rows with no `st_` value.
- One responder per row, including any filter that sets a value to zero; responders are never combined within a row or a variable.
- The study's main series is primary, and a second responder, instrument or diary on the same occasion is a tagged block.
- Block tags are `diary`, `parent`, `child`, `device` and `recall`, and every block maps `st_measure_type`, `st_measure_name` and `st_responder`.
- A `recall` block covers the same occasion with a different reference period; its other variables belong to the occasion, so concurrent analyses exclude it.
- Waves, and country-cycles of optional modules, with no disaggregated screen item are dropped in the tidier, so expressions need no wave conditions.
- The school-work part of an all-device item split by purpose counts as disaggregated (educational use) and keeps a wave, and an all-device item restricted to leisure keeps one too, though it fills only `st_leisure`.
- Hours of violent watching or gaming count as disaggregated and keep a wave; a violent-content index that gives no hours does not keep a wave on its own.
- Hours of educational programmes count as disaggregated and keep a wave, as violent hours do.
- Household TV-on time (hours the TV is on at home) describes the home, not the child: it fills no row and does not keep a wave.
- An age at a first own phone or at first screen use describes the child's history, not current use: it goes to `fam_firstphone_age` or `fam_firstscreen_age`, fills no `st_*` row and does not keep a wave.

### Scoring scales

- Higher means more of the construct the description names; reverse source scales to match.
- Rebase in the expression (subtract the item count for 1-based items; reverse as (min + max) - x) and record both in notes.
- Set sentinel and off-scale item codes to NA (`na_if()`, `%in%` valid codes) before scoring, and check the observed range against the published range.
- Before mapping a study-supplied total, check its keying (every item correlates positively with the total) and rescore from items if it fails.
- A named-instrument row takes the full published form on its published response scale and scoring, or a study composite equated to that metric (partial).
- Short forms, item subsets, adapted forms and the same items on another response scale go to the generic row, and the named row is incompatible.
- When the generic row already takes another scale given on the same occasion (a full named form is repeated there first), such a form stays partial on its named row instead, so its score is kept.
- Where the construct has no generic row (e.g. KIDSCREEN-10, Subjective Happiness Scale), the same items on another response scale stay partial on the named row.
- Short or adapted SDQ and CBCL parent forms stay partial on their named rows, as for a construct with no generic row, and never move to a generic `_parent` row; an adapted SDQ parent prosocial subscale still repeats on `beh_prosocial_parent`.
- Exceptions: `mh_dep_scl_self` takes SCL-90-R short forms, the RCADS-25 depression items map to `mh_dep_rcads_self`, and mean-item CBCL rows take item subsets as partial.
- A generic ('any instrument') row takes a multi-item scale administered for the construct.
- On a generic row the status reflects construct fit only; short forms, subsets and adapted scoring are compatible when the `*_measure` row describes them.
- When a named self-report row is mapped, repeat its expression on the generic row.
- When a single-construct named parent-report row is mapped (the BASC-2, SCAS, SCARED and SMFQ parent rows), repeat its expression on the generic `_parent` row of its construct; SDQ scores other than the parent prosocial subscale, and CBCL syndrome and composite scores, stay on their own rows and never repeat, and only the CBCL DSM-oriented scales and Total Problems, which have no CBCL row, map to the generic `_parent` rows.
- The SDQ parent prosocial subscale is the one SDQ parent score that repeats: when `beh_prosocial_sdq_parent` is mapped, repeat its expression on `beh_prosocial_parent`, as the self-report subscale repeats on `beh_prosocial_self`.
- The SDQ teacher prosocial subscale repeats in the same way: when `beh_prosocial_sdq_teacher` is mapped, repeat its expression on `beh_prosocial_teacher`; the other SDQ teacher scores stay on their own rows and never fill a generic `_teacher` row.
- Teacher's Report Form Internalizing, Externalizing and Total Problems and its DSM-oriented anxiety and affective scales fill the generic `_teacher` rows of their construct, its Aggressive Behavior syndrome fills `beh_agg_teacher` and its attention scales go to the teacher attention rows (`beh_atten_teacher`, `beh_hyper_teacher`, `beh_adhdsymp_teacher`) by their content; its anxious/depressed, withdrawn/depressed, somatic complaints, social problems, thought problems and rule-breaking syndromes and its DSM-oriented somatic, oppositional and conduct scales have no teacher row and are named as unused.
- Standardise generic rows, single-rating rows and raw-score rows within dataset at analysis, and within wave where the scale or form changes.
- `*_measure` rows read '\<instrument>, \<k> of \<K> items, \<a>-\<b> item scoring (range \<min>-\<max>), \<sum|mean>', then the reversed items and any change of response format or recall period.
- `*_measure` rows are inferred, entity study, filled in waves (or country-cycles) where the scale was given, a constant when every wave fielded it, and NA elsewhere, never 'Unknown' as a filler.
- `hlth_bmi_measure` and `cog_earlylang_measure` are the exceptions: they are entity participant and their value follows the row (the height-and-weight source, or the child's form or age interval), and `hlth_bmi_measure` is compatible where a source column records the source per row.
- A `*_measure` row says 'Unknown' only when a score exists but its instrument cannot be identified.
- Use a study-supplied score as released and record its missing-item rule ('rule not documented' if unknown).
- A released score prorated or averaged over answered items is used only where at least half the scale's items were answered.
- A favourite-titles index counts the titles the respondent answered about as its items: a title counts where any per-title answer (frequency, time or rating) is given, and the index is used only where at least half of those titles were rated, so a respondent who names fewer titles is not penalised.
- Sums computed in the expression are complete-case (`+`), unless the manual prescribes proration.
- **SDQ rule:** items scored 0-2 (not true 0, somewhat true 1, certainly true 2), items 7, 11, 14, 21 and 25 reversed, subscale = mean of answered items × 5 rounded half up with `floor(x + 0.5)`, NA when fewer than 3 of 5 are answered.
- Where the SDQ items are released, check the study's subscale against them: keep it if it follows the SDQ rule, otherwise gate or recompute it from the items.
- Where the SDQ items are not released, use the study's subscale after checking its range and reversals, and say in notes that the missing-item rule could not be verified.
- An SDQ subscale is incompatible when fewer than 3 of its items were administered, and total difficulties is scored only when all four difficulty subscales are.
- Pool the SDQ 2-4 and 4-17 parent forms and record the form version.
- SDQ self rows keep every age administered and record the age range and under-11 share.
- SDQ externalising and internalising are unavailable ('Derive at analysis from the subscale rows.') unless only the composite is released.
- Marsh's Self-Description Questionnaire (SDQ-I, SDQ-II, SDQ-III) is not the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire and never fills a `*_sdq_*` row: its General School (SDQ-III General Academic), subject and same-sex or peer-relations scales go to the self-concept rows, its parent-relations scale goes to `fam_parentchild_rel_self`, its Total Academic score is a composite across subjects and fills none, its general-self scale goes to `wb_selfesteem_self`, and its physical appearance scale goes to `wb_bodyesteem_self`.
- Body-satisfaction, body-esteem and appearance self-concept scales go to `wb_bodyesteem_self` (a scale that mixes appearance with physical-ability items is partial), never to `wb_selfesteem_self`; single body or appearance satisfaction items stay on `wb_domainsat_appearance_self`, perceived body size on `wb_bodyimage`, and physical-ability or athletic self-concept scales and figure-rating scores fill no row.
- **CBCL rule:** mean of the answered 0-2 items of the form's scale, NA when fewer than 80% of administered items are answered, codes outside 0-2 set to NA.
- CBCL composites take the mean over the union of component items, gate each component at 80%, and follow the form's published grouping.
- `beh_cbcl_measure` records the form, items administered of the published total per scale, the scoring and the missing rule, one value per wave where forms differ.
- **Parent-scale rule:** the generic `_parent` scale rows take a published scale or subscale of a parent- or carer-rated instrument as the raw sum or mean the instrument defines, keyed so higher means more problems, with a T-score or standard score only where no raw score is released (partial) and never a percentile or cut-off band.
- The parent-scale rule also covers `beh_selfreg_parent`, `beh_emotdysreg_parent`, `beh_prosocial_parent`, `beh_socialskills_parent`, `beh_problematicuse_parent` and the temperament rows, but the self-regulation, prosocial and social-skills rows run higher = more self-regulation, more prosocial behaviour and more social skills, the temperament rows higher = more of the trait, and temperament effortful-control scales map to `beh_selfreg_parent` as partial while other temperament scales map only to the temperament rows.
- Parent- or carer-rated temperament scales other than effortful control go to `beh_temp_negaffect_parent` (negative affectivity) or `beh_temp_surgency_parent` (surgency or extraversion), described in `beh_temp_measure`: the broad factor, or the mean of all the form's facets of it, is compatible; some of those facets, a single facet, a composite with off-construct items or the matching scale of another temperament instrument is partial; orienting, shyness-only and cooperativeness scales fill no row.
- Social-skills totals go to `beh_socialskills_self`, and social-skills or social-competence totals to `beh_socialskills_parent` and `beh_socialskills_teacher`; self-rated social-competence and social-acceptance scales stay on `wb_selfconcept_social_self`; where only facet subscales are released, the mean of the released facets other than self-control (an empathy facet of the instrument included) is partial, a self-control subscale stays on `beh_selfreg_parent` or `beh_selfreg_self` (a teacher-rated one fills no row), and prosocial, peer-problem and peer-interaction scales never fill them.
- `beh_problematicuse_parent` takes parent- or carer-rated scales of the child's problematic screen use and shares `beh_problematicuse_measure` with `beh_problematicuse_self`, one segment per row; a parent-completed form of an instrument written for self-report is partial, and a parent's own problematic use never fills it.
- `beh_emotreg_parent` also follows the parent-scale rule, keyed higher = better regulation: it takes emotion regulation competence scales, `beh_emotdysreg_parent` takes dysregulation scales, a study with both kinds fills both, and neither kind is ever reversed onto the other's row.
- The parent-scale rule and the two-scales rule of the `_parent` rows also cover the generic `_teacher` scale rows (`beh_aggphys_teacher`, `beh_aggrel_teacher`, `beh_agg_teacher`, `beh_victphys_teacher`, `beh_victrel_teacher`, `beh_vict_teacher`, `beh_atten_teacher`, `beh_hyper_teacher`, `beh_adhdsymp_teacher`, `beh_ext_teacher`, `beh_prosocial_teacher`, `beh_socialskills_teacher`, `mh_int_teacher`, `mh_anx_teacher`, `mh_dep_teacher` and `mh_totalprob_teacher`), applied to the teacher's ratings and keyed so higher means more of the behaviour, problem, victimisation or skill the row names; one shared `beh_teacher_measure` records the instrument, rater and scoring of each.
- The generic `_teacher` scale rows take ratings of the child by a school teacher or an early-childhood educator (preschool, kindergarten or child-care staff, a paid home-based care provider included), with the rater named in `beh_teacher_measure`; ratings by parents and family carers, a relative who looks after the child included, never fill them.
- The same teacher rules (the parent-scale rule, the two-scales rule and the rater scope) cover `cog_execfunc_teacher` and `acc_schoolengage_teacher`, which record the instrument and rater in `cog_execfunc_measure` and `acc_schoolengage_measure` instead of `beh_teacher_measure`.
- Where an instrument releases a parent score on its full response scale beside a dichotomised one, the `_parent` row takes the full-response-scale score.
- Single parent-rated items, study checklists with no published scoring, temperament scales other than effortful control (outside the temperament rows), teacher ratings and the symptom or criteria counts of skip-structured diagnostic interviews never fill a generic `_parent` row; the row is incompatible, naming them.
- With only parent problem scales in hand (attention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, oppositional, conduct or broadband problem scales, SDQ and CBCL scores included), `beh_selfreg_parent` and `beh_emotdysreg_parent` are incompatible, naming the scales and the rows that hold them.
- The same holds for `beh_emotreg_parent`, which is also incompatible with only dysregulation scales in hand, for the self-report twins `beh_selfreg_self`, `beh_emotreg_self` and `beh_emotdysreg_self` with only problem scales in hand, and for `beh_emotreg_self` with only dysregulation scales in hand; the self-report twins also follow their parent rows' rules for temperament, executive-function and mixed-facet scales.
- Inattention-only scales go to `beh_atten_parent` and hyperactivity-impulsivity-only scales to `beh_hyper_parent`; a scale that mixes the two, and a released combined ADHD total or index that is not the sum of those two rows, go to `beh_adhdsymp_parent`, and a sum of the two rows is derived at analysis.
- The self-report ADHD rows split the same way: inattention-only scales go to `beh_atten_self`, hyperactivity-impulsivity-only scales to `beh_hyper_self`, and a scale that mixes the two, or a released combined total that is not the sum or mean of those two rows, to `beh_adhdsymp_self`, with a sum or mean of the two rows derived at analysis; SDQ hyperactivity/inattention stays on `beh_hyper_sdq_self` and trait impulsivity scales on `beh_impulsivity_self`.
- The teacher attention rows split the same way: inattention-only scales go to `beh_atten_teacher`, hyperactivity-impulsivity-only scales to `beh_hyper_teacher`, and a scale that mixes the two, or a released combined ADHD index that is not the sum or mean of those two rows, to `beh_adhdsymp_teacher`; a subscale with academic-skill items is partial on `beh_atten_teacher`.
- Oppositional-defiant scales go to `beh_opp_parent` and conduct-disorder scales to `beh_conduct_parent`; a study with both fills both; a scale that mixes oppositional with conduct items or measures aggression alone goes to `beh_conduct_parent` as partial; anger or irritability mood scales fill neither row.
- The self-report rows split the same way: oppositional-defiant scales go to `beh_opp_self` and conduct-disorder or delinquency scales to `beh_conduct_self`, a scale mixing the two goes to `beh_conduct_self` as partial, and both share `beh_ext_measure` with `beh_ext_self`, one segment per row; for the Youth Self-Report the DSM-oriented Oppositional Defiant and Conduct Problems scales map and the Rule-Breaking Behavior syndrome is named as unused.
- Where a parent scale's item set changes with the child's age, the `_parent` row takes the released raw score (compatible), `beh_parent_measure` gives the item counts by age, and the score is standardised within dataset and age band at analysis.
- When two scales qualify for one generic `_parent` row on the same occasion, map the named-row repeat first, then a compatible scale over a partial one, then the scale with the most non-missing values, and name the others as unused.
- PedsQL items are transformed 0-4 to 100-0 and averaged when at least half are answered.
- BPAQ-SF rows take the published items, never a study's own syntax, and need all three items.
- `beh_anger_self` takes self-report anger and anger-control-problem scales, described in `beh_anger_measure`: a mapped `beh_agganger_bpaq_self` repeats there, other forms of the BPAQ anger items go there instead of the named row, anger outbursts at objects (throwing, breaking or slamming things) are anger-control content, a scale that mixes anger with urges or acts to harm people (a hostility scale, or an anger scale that adds them) is partial, and parent- or teacher-rated anger scales fill no row.
- Aggressive cognitions have one generic self-report row each, sharing `beh_aggcog_measure`: `beh_aggbeliefs_self` takes the total approval score of a normative-beliefs scale (a study's own items on how acceptable fighting is as partial, scored as the share of approving answers), `beh_agghostattrib_self` the share or count of hostile intent attributions over ambiguous-provocation vignettes, and `beh_aggfantasy_self` an aggressive-fantasy frequency scale; cognitive hostility scales (`beh_agghostility_bpaq_self`) and aggressive-behaviour scales stay on the aggression rows, anger scales and hostility scales that mix anger with urges or acts to harm people go to `beh_anger_self`, and none of these fills the aggressive-cognition rows.
- Subject composites (grades, teacher and parent ratings) average every academic subject reported, not arts, PE or ICT, and need every component (partial).
- Self-concept and self-efficacy are never averaged across subjects: maths, verbal and science self-concept go to their own rows, a composite across subjects fills no self-concept row, and subject self-efficacy scales are incompatible on `wb_selfefficacy_academic_self`, which does take a published academic efficacy subscale whose items each name a subject.
- Respondent suffixes are literal, respondents are never coalesced, and the CBCL and BASC-2 rows are parent report only.
- `_parent` rows take a rating of the child by a parent or other family caregiver (ratings by preschool, kindergarten or child-care staff fill only the teacher rows), with the rater named in the notes, and a score averaged over two parents' ratings is the one exception to never coalescing respondents: it maps as partial, with the averaging named in `beh_parent_measure` or in the row's own measure row (e.g. `beh_temp_measure`, `beh_problematicuse_measure`).
- The family rows of the parent's own practices and of family relationships (`fam_parenting_warmth_parent`, `fam_parenting_harsh_parent`, `fam_parenting_inconsistent_parent`, `fam_monitoring_parent`, `fam_functioning_parent`, `fam_conflict_parent`, `fam_parentchild_rel_parent`, `fam_parentchild_conflict_parent`) are not ratings of the child: they take a published scale or subscale, or a study's released scale, as compatible and the mean of a study's own two or more graded items as partial, never single items, and where two parents each report on one occasion they take the parent recorded in `parent_respondent` (the screen-time reporter, else the main parent interview) and name the other as unused, never an average.
- Their self-report twins (`fam_monitoring_self`, `fam_functioning_self`, `fam_conflict_self`) follow the same rules for the child's report; `fam_parentchild_rel_self` averages the child's ratings of mother and father where both are rated; true/false items count toward a study's item mean only on the two monitoring rows; and family functioning and family conflict, or parent-child closeness and conflict, keep separate rows that are never reversed onto each other.
- The family scale rows share three measure rows, one segment per mapped row naming the informant: `fam_parenting_measure` (warmth, harsh and inconsistent discipline and both monitoring rows), `fam_functioning_measure` (functioning and conflict) and `fam_parentchild_measure` (the parent-child rows).
- Cognitive rows take the age-normed score the study releases: standard score (mean 100, SD 15), T-score (50, 10) or scaled score (10, 3).
- Raw, ability or number-correct scores map only when no normed form exists, as partial; percentiles, age-equivalents and normative classifications never map.
- `cog_earlylang_parent` is the exception: parent-report early-language scales change items with the child's age and publish age norms only as percentiles or cut-off zones, which never map, so the row takes the raw ASQ-3 Communication area score or CDI word count as compatible, and the form and age interval are recorded in `cog_earlylang_measure` for standardisation within dataset and form or age interval at analysis.
- `fam_home_total` takes the released raw total of a published HOME Inventory form, short forms included, and `fam_home_cogstim` and `fam_home_emotsupport` the released subscales of a HOME short form; full-form subscales are used only through the total, a standard score only where no raw score is released (partial), and `fam_home_measure` lists the forms by age group so the scores are standardised within dataset and form at analysis.
- Never mix score forms within a row across waves; the executive-function rating rows (`cog_execfunc_parent`, `cog_execfunc_teacher`, `cog_execfunc_self`) are the exception: their instrument or score form may change between waves, as partial, standardised within wave.
- NIH Toolbox rows take the age-corrected standard score (uncorrected only as partial), and the BASC-2 executive-function row takes the T-score; never the fully corrected T-score.
- BAS II subtests are given individually, so there is no GCA for `cog_iq_fullscale`; map T-scores for the cognitive subtests and standard scores (mean 100, SD 15) for the achievement scales, with ability scores only as a partial fallback.
- The BAS II Word Reading and Number Skills rows also fill the generic literacy and numeracy rows with the same score.
- NEPSY rows take the same-named subtest from either edition; record the edition and age at testing.
- Only the child's own test maps; tests the caregiver took never map to child rows.
- A parent's or carer's own answers on an emotion regulation or self-control scale never fill the child emotion regulation or self-control rows.
- Executive-function rating scales, parent-, teacher- or self-rated, run higher = more difficulties, so scales keyed higher = better are reversed, and never pool with performance tasks.
- Executive-function rating scales that have their own row (BRIEF, BASC-2 executive functioning) stay whole on it: their scales and indexes, any form, never fill `beh_selfreg_parent`, `beh_emotdysreg_parent`, `beh_emotreg_parent` or the self-report regulation rows (`beh_selfreg_self`, `beh_emotreg_self`, `beh_emotdysreg_self`), and a mapped BRIEF or BASC-2 parent row repeats unchanged on `cog_execfunc_parent`.
- Other executive-function questionnaires go to the generic rating rows of their informant (`cog_execfunc_parent`, `cog_execfunc_teacher`, `cog_execfunc_self`, sharing `cog_execfunc_measure`) as their total, global or cognitive executive-function composite, with subscale and index scores named as unused; such a questionnaire also gives its inhibitory-control subscale to `beh_selfreg_parent` (a self-report form to `beh_selfreg_self`), partial.
- Child-performed attention, set-shifting, inhibitory-control, working-memory and processing-speed tasks go to the generic task rows (`cog_atten_task`, `cog_flex_task`, `cog_inhib_task`, `cog_wm_task`, `cog_speed_task`), one task per dataset per row, with the task described in the matching `*_measure` row; a mapped NIH Toolbox, NEPSY or Digit Span row repeats there, forward-only span tasks are partial on `cog_wm_task`, and Trail Making part A stays on `cog_atten_task`.
- Cross-out or cancellation subtests released within a processing-speed index or cluster go to `cog_speed_task` (compatible), while the visual search and cancellation tasks of attention batteries stay on `cog_atten_task`.
- Child-performed non-verbal reasoning tests (progressive matrices and the matrix-reasoning subtests of standardised batteries) go to `cog_nonverbalreason_task`, one test per dataset, described in `cog_nonverbalreason_task_measure`; as an exception to the raw-score rule above, it takes the age-normed score where one is released and otherwise the raw number correct, both compatible, standardised within dataset and age band at analysis, and a mapped BAS Picture Similarities row repeats there as partial.
- Child-performed vocabulary tests go to `cog_vocab_receptive_task` (picture-pointing tests) and `cog_vocab_expressive_task` (picture-naming and word-definition tests), one test per dataset per row, a test in a language of the country of data collection first, described in `cog_vocab_task_measure`; as on `cog_nonverbalreason_task`, an exception to the raw-score rule above, they take the age-normed score where one is released and otherwise the raw number correct, both compatible, a mapped PPVT, BPVS, NIH Toolbox Picture Vocabulary or BAS Naming Vocabulary row repeats there, broader language scales of a developmental battery are partial, and parent-report checklists stay on `cog_earlylang_parent`.
- Parent-rated self-regulation scales (`beh_selfreg_parent`) never pool with Head-Toes-Knees-Shoulders or other task scores, which stay on `beh_selfreg_htks` and the task rows.
- Self-report scales presented as self-control or self-regulation, temper and anger control included, go to `beh_selfreg_self` (partial where the scale adds coping or problem-solving items), scales presented as poor emotional self-control go to `beh_emotdysreg_self`, scales presented as impulsivity stay on `beh_impulsivity_self`, and ADHD symptom scales go to the self-report ADHD rows; none of them pools with a task or a parent rating.
- Emotion regulation strategy scales keep their facets apart: expressive suppression goes to `beh_emotreg_suppression_self` and cognitive reappraisal to `beh_emotreg_reappraisal_self`, each keyed higher = more use of the strategy, never summed into one score and never pooled with the regulation rows `beh_emotreg_self` and `beh_emotdysreg_self`.
- Self-report emotion regulation follows the parent pair: competence scales go to `beh_emotreg_self` (higher = better regulation) and dysregulation scales to `beh_emotdysreg_self` (higher = more dysregulation), a study with both kinds fills both, and neither kind is ever reversed onto the other's row; awareness of one's own feelings goes to `beh_emotaware_self`, and difficulties-keyed awareness and clarity scales are never reversed onto it.
- General distress inventories (Kessler, Malaise Inventory, GHQ-12) map to their own rows and repeat on the generic `mh_distress_self`, never to the depression or anxiety rows.
- A parent's or carer's own depression, anxiety and distress scales go to `fam_parent_dep`, `fam_parent_anx` and `fam_parent_distress`, never to a child row: the mother figure's score, else the responding parent's or primary caregiver's, named in `fam_parent_mh_measure`, with another parent's score unused; distress inventories go to `fam_parent_distress` only, an instrument with published depression and anxiety subscales gives those subscales and leaves its total and stress subscale unused, and a scale from a pregnancy or an earlier wave is never carried to a later one.
- Social-anxiety scales and the published social-anxiety or social-phobia subscales of broader instruments go to `mh_socanx_self`, a dedicated scale before a subscale on the same occasion, and a scale presented under another name (e.g. shyness or social withdrawal) whose items are shyness or social-anxiety items fills it as partial.
- Only a social-anxiety scale or subscale also fills `mh_anx_self`, as partial, and only where no broader anxiety scale was given on that occasion; a shyness or social withdrawal scale never does.
- Published negative-affect scales (e.g. PANAS negative affect) go to `wb_negaffect_self`, never to the distress, depression or anxiety rows; a study's own set of negative-feeling items with no published scoring (a survey's feelings battery, diary or experience-sampling emotion ratings) is a study checklist on `mh_distress_self`, partial; subscales and totals of depression, anxiety, stress or distress inventories stay on the mental-health rows and fill neither affect row.
- Published positive-affect scales go to `wb_posaffect_self`, compatible, and a study's own set of two or more positive-feeling items with no published scoring (the positive half of a feelings battery, diary or experience-sampling positive emotion ratings) fills it too, partial, while the matching negative-feeling items stay on `mh_distress_self`; energy or vitality items do not count as positive feelings, and an experience-sampling or diary composite is the person mean over the burst.
- Plausible-value scales use the first plausible value only.
- Achievement tests take one domain per row (`acc_academachment_stdtest` records its domain); age-normed standard or scale scores are compatible and raw scores partial.
- Record the test, subtest and score type, and standardise test scores within dataset and wave at analysis.
- Social-support rows take only items on support the child receives or can call on (help, understanding, someone to talk to or confide in).
- Parenting behaviours and family involvement are incompatible on the support rows, and a published support subscale that mixes in companionship items is partial.
- School belonging takes only scales presented as belonging or connectedness; teacher- or classmate-support scales and school-environment quality-of-life subscales are incompatible.
- Multi-item engagement and attitude-to-school scales go to `acc_schoolengage_self` (teacher ratings to `acc_schoolengage_teacher`), keyed higher = more engagement, and belonging scales stay on `acc_schoolbelonging_self`, a study with both filling both; a total that adds other facets (e.g. school adjustment with peer-relationship subscales) is partial and a released engagement or learning subscale is mapped before it, and single liking, caring and homework items stay on their single-item rows.
- Multi-item academic-stress and school-burnout scales go to `acc_schoolstress_self`, keyed higher = more stress; a burnout total that adds cynicism, inadequacy or reversed vigour items is partial, the single pressure item stays on `acc_schoolpressure_self` (a study with both fills both), and test-anxiety and general perceived-stress scales never fill it.

### Single items

- **Frequency-item rules** (`mh_*_self` rows with Always to Never): self-reported frequency ratings only; truth, agreement, intensity and distress ratings are incompatible, item named.
- Map anchors by wording: never, none, not at all -> Never; almost never, hardly ever, seldom, less than 1 day -> Rarely; sometimes, occasionally, some of the time, several days -> Sometimes; often, more than half the days -> Often; always, almost always, all of the time, nearly every day -> Always.
- An anchor steps down one label when the source has an intensified anchor above it ('quite often' under 'very often' -> Sometimes; 'most of the time' under 'always' -> Often), and a top anchor above a source 'often' -> Always.
- Day counts without wording map by share of a known recall window: 0 -> Never, up to 10% -> Rarely, up to 35% -> Sometimes, up to 70% -> Often, above 70% -> Always.
- Labels the source cannot reach stay unused and are named in notes; a source with fewer than five levels is proximate; a wording mismatch is partial.
- Record the recall period on every frequency row; it does not change the status there.
- An item also scored in a scale may fill a single-item row when it is self-reported, frequency- or presence-rated and matches in wording; note 'also scored in \<row>'.
- Score rows take only published scale or subscale scorings, never an ad hoc sum of another instrument's items.
- **GAD-7 crosswalk:** not at all, several days, more than half the days, nearly every day -> Never, Sometimes, Often, Always (PHQ items the same).
- CES-D day bands <1, 1-2, 3-4, 5-7 -> Rarely, Sometimes, Often, Always; all, some, none of the time -> Always, Sometimes, Never.
- A measure of another person (a parent's own stress or diagnosis) is unavailable on a `_self` row.
- Always/Usually/Sometimes/Never rows take frequency scales only; degree, importance and agreement scales are incompatible.
- On those rows, map anchors by wording with the same positional step; a four-level source whose labels do not match maps by rank, proximate, with the anchors in notes.
- 'All/Most/Some of the time' = Always/Usually/Sometimes, and a negatively worded item is never reversed onto these rows.
- **Five-level collapse** onto Very good, Good, Average, Below average: top -> Very good, second -> Good, middle -> Average, two lowest -> Below average (proximate), from the full-resolution source item.
- The four HBSC-SCL single-item rows are named-instrument rows: unavailable ('HBSC-SCL not administered; see \<row>.') wherever neither the checklist nor the adaptation in the row's note was given, even when a related item is in hand.
- On school pressure, worry about school performance and test anxiety are related items (incompatible, item named), and a five-point pressure scale maps its top two levels to 'A lot'.
- A behaviour item that places a device in the bedroom is partial on `fam_bedroomscreen`, and a parent's technical time limit is partial on `fam_screenrules`.
- `fam_readto_time` takes hours per average day under the screen-time band rules, **Non-users** and the **Day-of-use rule**, so minutes on each day of reading are scaled by days read to per week / 7 and marked partial.
- A verbal reading frequency takes the days of its `fam_readto_freq` level (7, 4.5 or 1.5), and a frequency below weekly leaves `fam_readto_time` NA.
- `fam_coview_freq` takes screen use together with a parent or carer, or with one present and supervising, from any informant: verbal and share-of-time anchors map by the **Frequency-item rules** wording ('most of the time' under 'all of the time' is Often), day counts by their day-share cuts, and items asked per medium take the most frequent level.
- `fam_parent_screentime` takes the responding parent's own hours per average day under the screen-time band and **Non-users** rules, weekday and weekend items (5 × wd + 2 × we) / 7, and never the child's screen time.
- `fam_mediation_restrict`, `fam_mediation_active` and `fam_mediation_monitor` take a published mediation scale or a released study index (used only where at least half its items were answered) as compatible, and the mean of a study's own graded items, a single graded item or a measure limited to some media as partial, and `fam_mediation_monitor` also takes a household item answered once for all the household's children as partial; checking ratings or suitability before allowing use is restrictive, and checking afterwards or keeping track of what the child watches, plays or does online is monitoring.
- Yes/no rule items stay on `fam_screenrules` (amount or timing) or `fam_contentrules` (content) unless a published index counts them, co-use stays on `fam_coview_freq`, and where the child and a parent both report mediation, the screen-time respondent's report is used.
- `fam_contentrules` and `fam_mediation_technical` are TRUE/FALSE rows like `fam_screenrules` that record their items in their own notes: an item pooling content with amount or timing rules is partial on both `fam_screenrules` and `fam_contentrules`, a technical time limit is partial on `fam_screenrules` and also fills `fam_mediation_technical`, and filters, blocking and parental-control or tracking software fill only `fam_mediation_technical`.
- Monitoring of the child's screen use goes to `fam_mediation_monitor`, and general monitoring of the child's whereabouts, companions and activities goes to `fam_monitoring_parent` or `fam_monitoring_self`; neither ever fills the other.
- `fam_firstphone_age` takes the age the child got a first own mobile phone, and an item on smartphones only, the age first allowed to use a phone or the age at first use of one is partial.
- `fam_firstscreen_age` takes the age at first use of any screen; one device or activity (the earliest of those asked) or the current age minus a reported duration of use is partial, and both onset rows are NA where the child has not started, never 0 or the current age.
- `fam_siblings_n` counts all the child's siblings, resident or not: a count of the family's children that includes the child maps as the count minus one, counts of children living in the household or limited by age are partial, and a yes/no has-siblings item goes to `fam_siblings_any`, which is unavailable wherever the count is mapped ('Derive at analysis from fam_siblings_n.').
- Binary behaviour rows are TRUE for any occurrence (the lowest response above never) and FALSE for never; yes/no items map directly.
- A multi-item composite is TRUE if any answered item is positive, FALSE if every answered item is never, and NA if none is answered; study missing codes count as unanswered.
- Use self-report where it exists; a parent-reported occurrence item is partial.
- `beh_suspended` is the exception: a parent's report and school records of suspension or expulsion are compatible, and where two or more informants report on one occasion a compatible report is used over a partial one, then the screen-time respondent's report, as for `acc_graderepeated`.
- E-cigarette and vaping items go to `beh_vaping_self` whatever the content, and items pooling vaping with smoked tobacco are partial there and on `beh_tobacco_self`; illicit drugs other than cannabis, inhalants included, go to `beh_drugs_self`, where non-medical use of medicines and anabolic steroids are incompatible, named.
- `fam_physpunish` follows the binary behaviour rules but records a parent's behaviour, so a report from any informant is compatible for a bounded recall period; a typical-frequency item with no recall period, a corporal-punishment subscale and lifetime items are partial, and the row is never carried across waves.
- An item limited to one sub-type or setting of the behaviour is partial; school-based items are compatible on the bullying rows.
- Truth- or agreement-rated items (SDQ, CBCL, 'describes this child') never map to binary or frequency rows; frequency-rated instrument items (BASC-2, PedsQL) are judged on content.
- School rows (truancy, suspension, school and schoolwork satisfaction, parent-rated school performance, homework time, academic self-efficacy, academic and subject self-concept, self-reported school engagement and academic stress) are NA for respondents not enrolled in school or enrolled beyond secondary school.
- `acc_homework_time` takes homework time in hours per average day under the screen-time band rules, **Non-users** (0 where a filter says no homework is set or done) and the **Day-of-use rule**; a total for the whole weekend is halved to one weekend day before the 5:2 weighting (partial), an item on school days only is taken as the average day (partial), and an item on yesterday or one named day is partial.
- Study time that also counts revision, exam preparation or work set by a private tutor or cram school is partial on `acc_homework_time`; time spent attending school lessons, tutoring or cram classes, or an item that counts it, is incompatible; a homework item that names screens goes to `st_educational`; where a child and a parent both report, the child's report is used.
- Single-rating rows (life, domain, happiness and self-esteem ratings) record the scale points and anchor wording and reverse scales where the lowest number is best.
- Keep one response scale per dataset per single-rating row where possible; where it changes between waves, standardise within dataset and wave.
- The teacher behaviour ratings (`beh_agg_singleitem_teacher`, `beh_prosocial_singleitem_teacher`, `beh_atten_singleitem_teacher`, `beh_disrupt_singleitem_teacher`) record the scale points, anchors and recall period and keep one response scale per dataset where possible, like the single-rating rows, but are keyed so that higher means more of the behaviour the row names (more attention problems on `beh_atten_singleitem_teacher`).
- Where two teachers rated the child on the same row (the same item or scale), that row takes one teacher, the one who rates the child on the dataset's other teacher-rated rows (else the one with more ratings), and names the other as unused; two teachers' ratings are never averaged.
- Multi-item teacher scales, a study's own scored scale included, go to the generic `_teacher` scale rows and never to the single-item teacher rows, and a single teacher item never fills a generic `_teacher` row; a study's own teacher items with no released or documented score are incompatible, named.
- A teacher aggression or victimisation scale that mixes two or more forms (physical, relational, verbal), or mixes physical with oppositional or anger items, goes to `beh_agg_teacher` or `beh_vict_teacher`; on `beh_agg_teacher` a scale presented as aggression is compatible and a narrow externalising scale of aggressive, oppositional and anger items is partial.
- The physical and relational teacher rows take only scales whose items are all physical or all relational, and a scale that adds hyperactivity-impulsivity items, or a broad externalising scale or composite that adds rule-breaking items, fills no teacher aggression row and goes to `beh_ext_teacher`.
- Faces scales (completely happy to not at all happy) count as satisfaction ratings, and life as a whole always goes to `wb_lifesat_singleitem_self`.
- Diagnosis rows: Never = never told, Previously = told but not current, Currently = told and current; treatment or medication as the proxy for current is partial; items not attributed to a health professional are incompatible.
- A stem that pools educators with health professionals ('a doctor, other health care provider, or educator ever told you') counts as attributed to a health professional, with no loss of status.
- A binary ever-told item attributed to a health professional, with no current or previous split, maps told to Currently diagnosed and not told to Never diagnosed, partial; it does not fill the waves of a row whose other waves separate current from previous diagnosis, which stay NA, because a weaker item fills missed waves only on score rows standardised within wave.
- Where a wave skips children already reported told of a condition at an earlier interview, a skipped child whose latest earlier answer was told takes Currently diagnosed, partial, and the notes name the routing.
- Where a study asks separately about conditions one diagnosis row covers (e.g. ADD and ADHD, or autism and PDD), a child told of any is told, and currently has the condition if any told item is current.
- Diagnosis severity rows (`*_diagnosed_severity`) take a rated severity of the current condition; ratings of how much a condition affects learning or daily activities are incompatible.
- `hlth_chroniccond_diagnosed` applies the diagnosis rules to any long-standing physical condition a health professional diagnosed, and where conditions are asked as separate items a child told of any counted condition counts as told; hay fever, food allergy and eczema alone, and mental, developmental and learning conditions, do not count, and an any-condition flag that includes the mild allergic conditions is partial.
- `hlth_disability` is TRUE for an identified disability or a long-term limitation of activities by a health condition (compatible, or partial where the item pools physical with mental conditions), a registered disability or a frequency item on how often a health problem limits activities (TRUE above never; partial, or proximate where it pools emotional problems); learning, intellectual, developmental and speech items alone never count, and a long-standing illness item with no limitation wording is incompatible.

### Categorical recodes

- Emit `allowed_values` exactly, case included.
- Demographic and SES rows emit the literal "Unknown", never NA, on every row of a mapped dataset, including waves where the item was not asked and nothing is carried (`default = "Unknown"` or `coalesce(..., "Unknown")`).
- `state` is the exception (NA outside Australia), and so is `ses_hukou` (NA outside mainland China or where not asked).
- `region` takes the current ISO 3166-2 code of the first-level unit (state, province or equivalent), aggregating lower units the code list names; a study's grouping of first-level units takes the country code and the grouping's English name ('US: South'), proximate, and school location stands in for residence (proximate).
- Places the code list does not name (towns, municipalities, schools) are never placed in a region with outside data.
- Every Australian row also takes its AU- code in `region`, from the source that fills `state` (which is kept beside it), and every UK row takes its nation's code (GB-ENG, GB-SCT, GB-WLS, GB-NIR), in wholly Australian and wholly UK datasets as in multi-country ones.
- Academic, behaviour, mental-health and health categorical rows use NA, never Unknown (except `hlth_bmi_measure`, whose 'Unknown' marks a value whose source cannot be identified); don't know, not graded, pass/fail and not applicable codes are NA.
- A source code no document defines maps to Unknown on demographic rows and NA elsewhere, never to a real category.
- A category merging a real value with Other or unknown maps to the real value (Female or unknown -> Female; Other or unknown -> Other), proximate, merge named; a merged Other/prefer-not-to-say maps to Unknown.
- A group with no schema category folds into Other and is proximate.
- A Hispanic-origin item sets Hispanic only in US and Canadian samples; elsewhere the race, colour or ethnic-group item decides.
- Minority, indigenous and immigrant background are judged against the country of data collection; multi-country data use a dataset lookup keyed on site and source value, with the reference group in notes.
- `home_language` is judged against the languages official across the whole country of data collection or across a whole first-level region (state, province, nation, autonomous community), and a source that records only that another language is spoken, not whether the country language is too, takes 'Another language, country language not recorded'.
- The main language spoken at home, the participant's first language, a responding parent's own home language and a count of languages spoken are proximate on `home_language`; interview or survey language, a parent's first language and language proficiency are incompatible, and no language item fills ethnicity, minority or immigrant background.
- Derived rows use the same item, lookup, free-text resolution and carry-forward as their source: minority and indigenous follow ethnicity.
- Released 'other, specify' text is resolved through a dataset lookup; a bare nationality is Unknown.
- A participant-level characteristic is never a constant from study context; country is the exception, and so are `born_in_country` Yes (inferred) where recruitment at birth in the country guarantees it and `school_track` 'Not tracked' (inferred) where the design places every participant at an untracked school stage.
- Birthplace rows use the UK as a whole and count Hong Kong and Macao in their own right.
- Recurring vocabularies use one shared lookup each (ethnicity, education), and all three parent-education rows call the same lookup.

### Age and time

- Completed years take +0.5 (13 -> 13.5); a completed-year band a-b takes (a + b + 1) / 2; an open band takes its inclusive bound + 0.5.
- The +0.5 rule is for age only; open screen-time bands take their floor.
- Survey year minus birth year is adjusted by the fieldwork midpoint, and decimal age is derived where birth and interview months are released.
- `maternal_age` takes the mother figure's age at the occasion under these age rules: her age at the child's birth plus `age_years` is compatible, a responding parent whose relationship to the child is not recorded is partial, the father's age is incompatible, and an age asked at one wave fills other waves as that age plus the change in `age_years`, partial, the projection named.
- A single-age sample with no age item takes the centre of the sampled cohort's age at fieldwork, inferred.
- Single completed years and survey-year differences are compatible; multi-year bands, open bands holding more than about 5% of rows and design-assigned ages are partial or inferred; a birth date against an assumed reference date is partial.
- Ages above `max_value` are kept, eligibility is applied at analysis, and tidiers drop rows only to define the study population and the waves each participant attended.
- `data_year` takes the per-row interview year where released (compatible) or the survey's own year label (compatible); a year recoded from wave labels or documentation is inferred.
- A missing per-row date takes the wave's modal fieldwork year; a few such fills leave the row compatible, with the count in notes, and inferred is for waves whose year is assigned wholesale.
- Constants cite the fieldwork or design documentation that dates them or, under the publication fallback below, the publication or bound that dates them.
- Fieldwork timing documented by the study's investigators counts even when it sits outside the supplied documents (e.g. a project description or funding report), and each wave takes its documented year, inferred.
- Only where nothing documents when collection took place is `data_year` the year of the earliest publication reporting the data, one constant for every row, inferred, with that publication cited in notes (DR-0005).
- Where a publication reporting the data documents an upper bound on when collection ended (e.g. a received or submission date) in a year before that constant, the constant takes the earliest such bound's year instead, and the notes cite the bound.
- A single-occasion dataset leaves `wave` NA (unavailable); repeated cross-sections use the four-digit survey year.

### Multiple waves and carry-forward

- **Carry-forward:** sex, ethnicity, indigenous status, immigrant background, `born_in_country`, home language (`home_language`), derived minority and the early-life rows (`hlth_birthweight`, `hlth_preterm`, `hlth_breastfed`, `hlth_prenatalsmoking`) are carried within participant through one allowlisted helper in the expression; observed values stay, and missing or not-asked waves take the earliest observed value in wave order.
- The onset ages `fam_firstphone_age` and `fam_firstscreen_age` are carried the same way, except to a wave at which the child had not yet started (a 'not yet' answer there, or a carried age above the child's age at that wave), which keeps NA.
- Sex items take the participant's modal observed value at every wave, ties Unknown; gender-identity items stay as recorded.
- Parent education is always carried; household SES, family structure, maternal employment and `region` are carried across gaps of 12 months or less (inclusive) and are otherwise Unknown, and the sibling rows (`fam_siblings_n`, `fam_siblings_any`) the same way but otherwise NA; this fill is done in the tidier.
- `school_track` is carried within participant while the participant stays at the same school stage (lower or upper secondary), filled in the tidier, and never across the move between stages.
- `acc_graderepeated` carries an observed TRUE within participant to every later wave the participant attended, over a later FALSE too, filled in the tidier; a FALSE is never carried, forward or backward.
- A follow-up wave with no age item takes the nearest recorded age plus the documented interval, filled in the tidier, partial.
- Waves and country-cycles with no disaggregated screen item are dropped in the tidier.
- Tidiers drop a participant's rows for waves the participant did not attend.
- Survey design values fixed at sampling (stratum, cluster, design weight) are carried within participant to every wave without a wave prefix, so a participant stays in one stratum and cluster; a carried design weight is partial.
- The weight is the study's core release weight, and schools in a randomised trial are not survey clusters.
- `rct_arm` takes the allocated arm in any controlled trial, randomised or not (whole classes or schools assigned by the investigators included), with the allocation design in notes, and datasets that are not trials keep 'Not a randomised trial.'
- `family_id` takes the study's own family unit (a family, household, questionnaire or mother id) and `sample_component` the separately recruited sample a participant belongs to; both are constant within participant, NA where the dataset holds one participant per family or one sample, and neither is a stratum, cluster, wave or trial arm.
- Wave coverage alone never lowers a status; list the waves in notes.
- A second report on the same occasion is a tagged measure block, never a wave.
- A `*_measure` string appears only in waves where its scale was given.

### Sleep

- Time of falling or going to sleep to waking counts as hours asleep (compatible unless banded); bedtime or lights-out to waking is partial.
- Never subtract a separate sleep-latency item.
- An open sleep band takes the bound its label states, or half an hour beyond a neighbouring point label ('less than 6 hours' next to '6 hours' = 5.5).
- The share of answers in an open band does not lower the status.
- Keep durations under 4 or over 16 hours; they are screened at analysis.
- Single items on how often the child has trouble falling or staying asleep, wakes in the night or sleeps poorly go to `hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_self` or `hlth_sleepprob_singleitem_parent` under the **Frequency-item rules**, which the parent row applies to a parent's ratings; yes/no items, sleep-quality and 'enough sleep' ratings, latency, timing, daytime sleepiness and items blaming a cause such as screen use are incompatible, and the HBSC-SCL item stays on `wb_psychcomplaints_diffsleep`.
